configuration_map: No geometric configuration exists. The proof is purely number-theoretic, dealing with numbers in continued proportion and their factorizations. All objects are natural numbers; 'solid number' means a product of three factors (D7.17), and 'similar solid numbers' means solid numbers with proportional sides (D7.21). No points, lines, angles, or geometric figures appear.
skip_reason: Book 8 is number theory with no spatial configuration. Proposition 8.21 proves that if two mean proportionals fall between two numbers, those numbers are similar solid numbers. The entire proof consists of algebraic ratio manipulations and factorizations of natural numbers using Book 7 propositions (7.17, 7.19, 7.20, 7.33). There are no geometric or spatial claims to check.
